findings.issue: The script hardcodes `python3 -I`. Windows Git Bash and python.org installs typically expose `python`, not `python3`. The justfile handles this with an os_family switch. The CI `deps` job runs only on ubuntu-24.04, so there is no current breakage.
findings.recommendation: Document that the script is POSIX/ubuntu-only, or resolve the interpreter (`python3` if available, otherwise `python`) if it must run on Windows bash.

notes: Script review. Both scripts use `set -euo pipefail` and `python3 -I`. check-exact-pins.sh uses tomllib. Exit codes (0, 1, 2) match the documented contract. Marker parsing requires each marker exactly once, enforces the start-before-end order and rejects an empty list. It strips line whitespace, so the indented markers in docs/architecture.md:920-926 parse correctly. Package renames, [target.*] tables, dev and build dependencies, and `>=`/`<=` ranges are handled, and the self-test covers them. The `trap ... RETURN` in self_test is fine.
cargo-tree-gates.sh uses word-bounded grep patterns and fails on a `cargo tree` error. It only covers the two mimalloc rows; the remaining rows are deferred to r-3b, as the script header says.

CI workflow. All new actions are SHA-pinned with version comments. Every new step has timeout-minutes and the job has a 30-minute timeout. The `deps` job sets up Python from env.PYTHON_VERSION, which is needed for tomllib. I did not verify that PYTHON_VERSION is >= 3.11 in the workflow env.

Cargo.lock. The regeneration adds only clap-related packages: anstream, anstyle, anstyle-parse, anstyle-query, anstyle-wincon, clap, clap_builder, clap_derive, clap_lex, colorchoice, is_terminal_polyfill, once_cell_polyfill, strsim, utf8parse. No removals, and no existing package version changed (the diff showed no `-` lines).

required-features. Under default features, the sc-ai and sc-treesitter `cli` test targets and bins all build and run, so no test target is skipped. Under --no-default-features the `cli` integration tests and the bins are intentionally skipped, and only the lib unit tests and doctests run. That is by design, but a plain `cargo test --no-default-features` reports success without exercising the CLI. CI covers the default-feature path and the lib build, so there is no gap. The rust and python feature combinations are exercised by cargo hack --each-feature.
Mimalloc/clap source usage appears confined to the two binary crates; the sc-lint ownership rules for both pass.
